findings.title: Amendment 20261025 not propagated through the document — pre-amendment statements remain as present-tense design
findings.description:
The amendment block says "the sections below are rewritten to match," but several are not:

- **Technical Considerations → "Guide release coupling":** the parenthetical correctly says the fail-fast rule "moves to the prompt-delivery primitive," yet the very next sentence still reads "If cf selects the brownfield profile and the installed guide lacks it, `cf build` fails with a named error." Post-amendment `cf build` selects no profile — by the amendment's own bullet "`cf build` is pure again."
- **Dependencies:** "cf releases that select the brownfield profile require at least **v0.22.2**" describes a release condition that no longer exists after 268/271 (cf delivers the prompt by key; `cf build` never selects the profile).
- **Responsibility Split, row (c):** "CF writes the architecture doc **on both paths**. **With squadron present**, squadron 362's comprehension analysis is an input." There is only one path now — "Squadron is the only adoption path (PM decision 20261025)" — and squadron is always present.
- **Current State → `cf next` bullet:** "`WorkflowNavigator.detectFirstRunContext`. Treats sparse planning state as a fresh project." Slice 264 shipped brownfield-aware navigation and 270 removes it again; this bullet describes neither shipped state nor the reworked state.
- **Scope line:** still lists "brownfield-aware navigation" as scope, while the amendment states "`cf next` carries no adoption guidance: one line for an unadopted brownfield repo."
- **Anticipated Slices:** the "original plan, all shipped (260–267)" list includes "Detection and adoption state: … the persisted adoption state, and `cf build` selecting the `brownfield-adoption` profile" and "Brownfield-aware `cf next`: adoption steps while in progress" — both explicitly reversed by 269/270. Marking this block as historical in one preamble line does not stop a reader (or a slice-design agent) from taking the bullets under a heading titled "Anticipated Slices" as current design.

Each stale statement directly contradicts an amendment bullet, so a reader must reconcile the document by hand before designing a slice against it.

findings.title: After rework, CF ships a complete brownfield stack that nothing invokes, and the transition window misdirects users via the shipped guide
findings.description:
Two related dependency problems:

1. **All adoption value is parked behind an external deliverable with no fallback.** The amendment drops the CF-only path ("Squadron is the only adoption path") and parks adoption "until `sq onboard` exists." After 268–272, CF ships detection (271a), prompt delivery (271b), the retroactive-marker parser and checker rule (263, deliberately kept), and docs-map tolerance (267) — none of which any in-repo command invokes. The initiative's stated goal ("`cf next` points at the first piece of *new* work") is delivered by nothing in this repo. The document treats this as settled (PM decision) but never states what CF validates in the meantime: no slice runs detection end-to-end for a user after 268, and 273 (the only real adoption run) is parked behind the same external dependency.
2. **Guide/cf sequencing gap between 268 and 272.** The installed guide (v0.22.x, still the initiative minimum per Dependencies) contains a Brownfield Adoption prompt that per its own header "Context Forge selects it (profile `brownfield-adoption`) and appends an 'Adoption Facts' section after it" — i.e., it tells agents to run `cf build`, which 268 makes pure. 272 (which coordinates the guide fix and raises `MIN_GUIDE_VERSION`) *depends on* 268–271, so the repo ships a window where the shipped, version-gated guide instructs a workflow cf just deleted. Nothing in the architecture assigns an ordering or interim guard (e.g. shipping 272's guide coordination first, or gating the prompt until 272).

findings.title: The new sq → cf contract replaces `probe_version` with no versioning or compatibility mechanism
findings.description:
Technical Considerations ("Squadron contract stability") states that the probe contract was locked at `probe_version` 1 with field-level compatibility rules (non-breaking surface additions, null-means-unknown, non-zero exit semantics, CF treating unreadable output as "squadron unavailable"). The amendment replaces that with "cf's detection report and prompt delivery (slice 271), which squadron calls" — but the document specifies no equivalent for the new direction:

- No schema version or field-compatibility rule for the JSON report `sq onboard` will parse.
- No statement of what happens when squadron calls a cf older than the one that added the state command (the probe handled the reverse case; nothing handles "command not found" on the cf side).
- No error contract for the prompt-delivery primitive's failure modes from squadron's perspective (missing guide prompt is an error "never a reason to fall back" — but what does squadron do with that error?).

Slice 271's only mitigation is a risk line ("confirm it with the sq session before design is final"), which defers the entire cross-repo contract to slice design while this architecture still claims to own the cf/squadron responsibility split. The discipline that existed for the probe (locked contract, version field, tested field names) was dropped along with the probe rather than moved to the new boundary.

findings.title: Cross-repo write contracts into CF are claimed but no artifact is assigned to specify them
findings.description:
The amended design narrows cf's contact with squadron to "comprehension doc by filename and `docType`" plus detection/prompt primitives — yet the Responsibility Split still asserts two write-side contracts flowing *into* CF with no owner for their specification:

- **Initiative candidates row:** "Squadron 364's 'candidates adopt' writes CF's initiative-plan format and never sets the retroactive marker." Whoever writes CF's format needs a spec of that format's required shape and the marker-exclusion rule; nothing in Dependencies or Related Work names where that spec lives or when it lands (364 is "frozen until the handoff contract settles," but the settling artifact is not identified).
- **Retroactive marker row (d):** "squadron's pipeline gates … read slice status" and the marker "counts as complete for every 'done' check (CF's and squadron's pipeline gates)." The guide's retroactive-marker rule is explicitly "Still pending, both written after cf specifies them in slice design" — so the cross-repo read contract exists only as prose in this document until 263's spec ships, and squadron's consuming side has no named dependency on it at all.
- **Concept writer:** the shared `000-concept` row says "Exactly one writer per run" among two candidate writers (squadron 363 vs the guide's adoption prompt, run by whoever `sq onboard` hands the prompt to). The disambiguation rule (who yields when both are available) is not stated; "nothing overwrites an existing concept without the PM saying so" governs only re-runs, not the first run.

These are the places where the "cf orchestrates nothing / one point of contact" principle actually leaks, and they are the least specified part of the document.

findings.title: Related Work links to a review file that does not exist in this checkout
findings.description: The last line links `../reviews/260-review.arch.brownfield-adoption.md` ("CONCERNS, 11 findings. All findings are addressed in this revision"). There is no `project-documents/user/reviews/` directory, and a project-wide grep finds no such file — the "all findings addressed" claim is unverifiable from the repository, and the link is dead. Either the file should be committed alongside the revision or the reference dropped.

findings.title: Detection outcome 2 ("already planned") can permanently close the adoption path on partially-adopted repos
findings.description: Detection ordering says outcome 2 fires when "the repo holds a CF/SQ planning artifact (an initiative plan, an architecture doc or a slice plan). A concept on its own does not count," and this is derived from files every time. A repo that aborted mid-adoption — architecture derived but slice plan never written (i.e., exactly the state `adoption.state: in_progress` used to encode, removed by 269) — now classifies as "already planned," so `sq onboard` step 2 says "adoption doesn't apply" and there is no in-flow way to resume; only the opt-out (which makes it greenfield, the wrong direction) exists. 269's one-time notice covers obsolete stored values but not this file-state ambiguity. Worth an explicit rule (e.g. "already planned" requires both an architecture *and* a slice plan) before 269 deletes the state.
